name: Turkey Pasteurisation & Cooking Temperature Chart
secondary_keywords: turkey sous vide time and temperature
search_intent: Chefs, butchers, caterers, and holiday roast cooks looking for exact internal core temperatures and required holding times to achieve a 7D (7-log / 99.99999%) reduction of Salmonella in whole turkey, crowns, and ground turkey, both for traditional roasting and low-temperature sous-vide or combi-oven cooking.

competitors.title: FSIS Salmonella Lethality Guide (Appendix A) | USDA
competitors.weaknesses: Dense, complex 40-page technical PDF, virtually unusable in a commercial kitchen.

competitors.title: The Food Lab's Guide to Turkey Temperatures | Serious Eats
competitors.strengths: Engaging culinary science explanations and culinary tests.
competitors.weaknesses: Consumer-oriented, narrative blog format, lacks catering audit features, CSV export, and UK FSA regulatory alignment.

competitors.title: Turkey Temperature Guide - ThermoWorks
competitors.strengths: High-quality temperature charts and probe location graphics.
competitors.weaknesses: Static graphic primarily built to sell thermometers, no interactive weight-to-time roasting calculator.

competitors.title: Meat Temperature Guide & Salmonella Lethality | AmazingRibs
competitors.weaknesses: Ad-heavy layout, US Fahrenheit only, cumbersome mobile layout.

competitors.title: Cooking Turkey Safely | Food Safety Authority of Ireland
competitors.weaknesses: Rigid single-temperature rule (75°C instant), ignores scientifically proven low-temperature pasteurisation tables.

gap_analysis.what_they_have: Academic PDF tables or single-temperature static consumer blog posts.
gap_analysis.what_they_lack: Dual-mode interactive tool supporting statutory limits (75°C core / 82°C Scotland), weight-based commercial cook time calculations, precision sous-vide lethality dwell times, and instant A4 kitchen wall chart printing.
gap_analysis.what_we_offer: Interactive species/cut selector with dedicated Turkey Pasteurisation standards, weight calculator, probe positioning guide, and full 60°C to 75°C lethality time-temperature tables.
